about: Thresholds that turn evidence into pillar colours and ranked issue candidates, so two runs on the same evidence give the same rating. Edit the numbers here; the code does not change. Paths start with r. (resource_evidence.json), w. (windows_evidence.json) or n. (entra_evidence.json). A rule fires when every 'when' test is true and, if 'when_any' exists, at least one of those is true. A test on a missing value is false and its pillar is marked not measurable. 'ratio_of' compares a value with a share of another value.

rules.headline: Critical flaw on {r.backup_vulnerable.exploitable_now} domain-joined backup servers
rules.title: Backup servers exposed to critical remote-code-execution flaws
rules.finding: Veeam Backup & Replication build {r.backup_vulnerable.versions} runs on {r.backup_vulnerable.endpoints} servers; {r.backup_vulnerable.domain_joined} are joined to the production domain. This build is affected by {r.backup_vulnerable.cves} (CVSS 9.9), which let any authenticated domain user execute code on domain-joined backup servers. The fix shipped in 12.3.2.4165 (Veeam KB4771, Oct 2025). Other backup components are listed as CVE status not verified.
rules.why: Ransomware crews target backups first so the organization cannot recover without paying. A single phished employee password could be enough to reach them.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to 12.3.2.4165 or later within 7 days. Move backup servers to a separate workgroup or management domain, enforce immutable or offline copies, and test a full restore.
rules.action: Patch Veeam and isolate backup servers

rules.headline: Vulnerable backup software on {r.backup_vulnerable.endpoints} servers
rules.title: Backup software has a known critical flaw
rules.finding: Veeam Backup & Replication build {r.backup_vulnerable.versions} runs on {r.backup_vulnerable.endpoints} servers and is affected by {r.backup_vulnerable.cves}. None is joined to the production domain, which the advisory requires for exploitation, so the exposure is lower but the build is still out of date.
rules.why: Backups are what lets the organization recover without paying. An unpatched backup server is a standing risk.
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to 12.3.2.4165 or later and keep backup servers off the production domain.

rules.headline: {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} unprotected active devices; {r.stale7_split} silent >7 days
rules.title: {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} active devices have no endpoint protection
rules.finding: Defender device discovery sees {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} active Windows, Linux and Mac devices that are neither onboarded to Defender nor matched to an {r.edr_name} agent. They include {r.unprotected.of_which_servers} servers and {r.unprotected.of_which_end_of_life} end-of-life systems. Phones, inactive and duplicate records are excluded. Matching is by hostname, so a small number may be guest or personal devices.
rules.why: Attackers look for the one machine nobody is watching. Anything unprotected is a free foothold to start encrypting from.
rules.recommendation: Install the endpoint agent on, or isolate, every unprotected device, servers and end-of-life systems first. Alert when a new device appears without an agent.
rules.action: Agent or isolate the {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} unprotected devices
rules.outcome: No blind spots on the network

rules.headline: {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} unprotected active devices
rules.title: {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} active devices have no endpoint protection
rules.finding: Defender device discovery sees {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} active devices with no matching {r.edr_name} agent. Matching is by hostname, so a small number may be guest or personal devices.
rules.why: Attackers look for the one machine nobody is watching.
rules.recommendation: Install the endpoint agent on, or isolate, every unprotected device.
rules.action: Agent or isolate the unprotected devices
rules.outcome: No blind spots on the network

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.stale} agents silent for over {r.stale_window_text}
rules.title: {r.endpoint.stale} agents have not checked in for over {r.stale_window_text}
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.stale} of {r.endpoint.agents} agents have not checked in for more than {r.stale_window_text} ({r.stale7_split}). More than 10% of the fleet is silent, so coverage on paper is much better than coverage in practice.
rules.why: A device that has gone quiet may be switched off, lost or have its protection removed, and it will not stop an attack while it is silent.
rules.recommendation: Review silent agents weekly, remove retired devices and investigate any that are active on the network but silent to the agent.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.stale} agents silent for over {r.stale_window_text}
rules.title: {r.endpoint.stale} agents have not checked in for over {r.stale_window_text}
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.stale} of {r.endpoint.agents} agents have not checked in for more than {r.stale_window_text} ({r.stale7_split}).
rules.why: A device that has gone quiet may be switched off, lost or have its protection removed, and it will not stop an attack while it is silent.
rules.recommendation: Review silent agents weekly, remove retired devices and investigate any that are active on the network but silent to the agent.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.rtr_not_enabled} agents cannot be remotely contained
rules.title: Responders cannot remotely contain some hosts
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.rtr_not_enabled} CrowdStrike agents have Real-Time Response switched off, so responders cannot investigate or isolate them during an incident.
rules.why: In a ransomware event the first move is to isolate the host. Without remote response that has to be done by hand.
rules.recommendation: Enable Real-Time Response on every host.
rules.outcome: Any host can be isolated remotely

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.contained} hosts network-contained
rules.title: Hosts are network-contained
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.contained} CrowdStrike hosts are network-contained. That is either an incident response in progress or a containment that was never lifted.
rules.why: A contained host is cut off from the network and may signal an active incident.
rules.recommendation: Confirm with the SOC whether each containment is intentional and lift any that are stale.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.no_firewall_policy} agents without the firewall policy
rules.title: The endpoint firewall policy is not applied everywhere
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.no_firewall_policy} of {r.endpoint.agents} CrowdStrike agents do not have the firewall policy applied.
rules.why: Host firewall rules slow an attacker moving between machines.
rules.recommendation: Assign and verify the firewall policy on every host group.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.not_provisioned} agents not provisioned
rules.title: Some agents are not fully provisioned
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.not_provisioned} CrowdStrike agents are not in the Provisioned state, so they may not report reliably.
rules.why: An agent that is not fully installed may not protect or report.
rules.recommendation: Finish or repeat the install, or remove the record if the host is gone.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.no_sensor_update_policy} agents without a sensor-update policy
rules.title: Some sensors are not kept up to date
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.no_sensor_update_policy} of {r.endpoint.agents} CrowdStrike agents have no sensor-update policy applied, so they are not kept current.
rules.why: Old sensors miss new detections and can fall into reduced functionality after an OS update.
rules.recommendation: Assign a sensor-update policy to every host group.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.reduced_functionality} agents in reduced-functionality mode
rules.title: Some endpoint agents are running with reduced protection
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.reduced_functionality} of {r.endpoint.agents} CrowdStrike agents are in reduced functionality mode, which usually means the sensor is not fully loaded or the host is unsupported, so prevention is limited on those machines.
rules.why: A sensor that is only partly working leaves the host exposed while the console still shows it as covered.
rules.recommendation: Find why each agent is in reduced functionality mode (kernel or OS support, sensor version) and fix or replace it.
rules.outcome: Full protection on every covered device

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.no_prevention_policy} agents with no prevention policy applied
rules.title: Some endpoint agents have no prevention policy applied
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.no_prevention_policy} of {r.endpoint.agents} CrowdStrike agents have no prevention policy applied, so the sensor is installed but not actively blocking.
rules.why: Without an applied prevention policy the sensor cannot stop ransomware, only report it.
rules.recommendation: Assign a prevention policy to every host group and confirm it applies.
rules.action: Apply a prevention policy to every agent

rules.headline: {r.hardening_rules_failing_everywhere} anti-ransomware rules and LAPS not enabled fleet-wide
rules.title: Core anti-ransomware hardening is reported as switched off
rules.finding: {r.hardening_rules_failing_everywhere} Defender hardening rules are reported non-compliant on every assessed device, including {r.hardening_examples}. Credential Guard is off on {r.credential_guard_off} devices. Device Secure Score is {r.secure_score}. Because every rule fails on every device, the tenant may simply not report these policies: confirm the policy state before closing this item.
rules.why: These settings stop ransomware from spreading and from stealing administrator passwords once it is inside. Without them one infected laptop can reach many others.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the policy state, then enable the attack-surface-reduction rules (audit, then block) and LAPS, and turn on Credential Guard.
rules.action: Confirm and enable the attack-surface-reduction rules, LAPS and Credential Guard
rules.outcome: Ransomware spread and credential theft made much harder

rules.headline: End-of-life systems{r.remote_headline_tail}
rules.title: {r.remote_title}
rules.finding: {r.eol_total} devices run systems past end of support ({r.eol_text}); {r.approaching_eol_text}. {r.remote_sanctioned_text} {r.remote_other_sentence}
rules.why: Old systems no longer get security fixes, and every extra remote-access tool is another way in that has to be secured.
rules.recommendation: Retire or upgrade end-of-life systems, approve one set of remote-access tools and remove the rest.
rules.action: Retire end-of-life systems and standardise remote-access tools

rules.headline: {r.vulnerabilities.exploit_available_devices} devices with exploitable CVEs
rules.title: Exploitable vulnerabilities are widespread and aging
rules.finding: {r.vulnerabilities.exploit_available_devices} devices carry critical or high CVEs with a known exploit ({r.vulnerabilities.exploit_available_cves} CVEs); on {r.vulnerabilities.exploitable_older_than_30d_devices} the exposure is older than 30 days and on {r.vulnerabilities.exploitable_older_than_90d_devices} older than 90 days. {r.vulnerabilities.exploitable_critical_devices} devices have exploitable criticals. Main drivers: {r.vuln_drivers_text}. Only {r.vulnerabilities.servers_in_vulnerability_data} of {r.vulnerabilities.servers_in_edr} servers reports into Defender vulnerability management, so server exposure is largely unmeasured.
rules.why: Known exploits are what attackers use to get in. Every month an exposure stays open raises the odds it is used.
rules.recommendation: Set patch deadlines (critical exploitable in 14 days), enforce browser auto-update, remove retired software, and onboard servers to vulnerability management.
rules.action: Patch deadlines and browser auto-update; onboard servers to vulnerability management

rules.headline: {r.vulnerabilities.exploit_available_devices} devices with exploitable CVEs
rules.title: Devices carry vulnerabilities with known exploits
rules.finding: {r.vulnerabilities.exploit_available_devices} devices carry critical or high CVEs with a known exploit; {r.vulnerabilities.exploitable_older_than_30d_devices} for more than 30 days.
rules.why: Known exploits are what attackers use to get in.
rules.recommendation: Patch exploitable criticals first and enforce patch deadlines.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.mitigation_issues} agents not fully in Protect mode
rules.title: Endpoint agents are not fully in Protect mode
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.mitigation_issues} of {r.endpoint.agents} SentinelOne agents have the threat or suspicious mitigation mode set to something other than Protect ({r.endpoint.detect_only} on the threat policy, {r.endpoint.suspicious_detect_only} on the suspicious policy). {r.mitigation_sentence} {r.scanner_text}
rules.why: The product can see an attack but is told not to stop it, so a real intrusion would only be noticed afterwards.
rules.recommendation: Move every agent to Protect on both policies, servers first. Remove or approve any scanning tool, and review unmitigated detections.
rules.action: Move all agents to Protect on both policies

rules.headline: {r.signin_headline}
rules.title: Admin portals and tenant sign-ins rely on passwords alone too often
rules.finding: {r.signin_sentence} {r.mfa_policy_text} {r.legacy_sentence} There are {r.identity.global_admins} Global Administrators. {r.signin_limits}
rules.why: A stolen password is the most common way in. Administrator access without a second factor lets an attacker take over the tenant.
rules.recommendation: Require MFA for all users and for every admin portal through conditional access, block legacy authentication, and review risky sign-ins.
rules.action: Require MFA for admin portals and all users through conditional access

rules.headline: {n.signins.single_factor_share_pct}% of successful sign-ins single-factor
rules.title: Most sign-ins use a password alone
rules.finding: {n.signins.single_factor_share_pct}% of successful sign-ins ({n.signins.singleFactorOk} of {n.signins.successful}) were single-factor.
rules.why: A stolen password is the most common way in.
rules.recommendation: Require MFA for all users through conditional access.

rules.headline: No policy enforces MFA for Global Administrators
rules.title: Nothing forces administrators to use MFA
rules.finding: No enabled conditional-access policy requires MFA for Global Administrators. {r.identity.global_admins} Global Administrators exist. Report-only and risk-based policies were not counted.
rules.why: An administrator with only a password lets one stolen credential take over the whole tenant.
rules.recommendation: Require MFA for all administrator roles on every app through an enforced conditional-access policy.
rules.action: Enforce MFA for every administrator role
rules.outcome: Administrator accounts need a second factor

rules.headline: The all-users MFA policy excludes directory roles
rules.title: The MFA policy for all users excludes privileged roles
rules.finding: The strictest policy requiring MFA for all users excludes {r.conditional_access.mfa_all_users_exclusions.roles} directory roles, which are usually the most privileged accounts.
rules.why: Exempting privileged roles removes the protection from exactly the accounts attackers want.
rules.recommendation: Remove role exclusions from the MFA policy and use a break-glass group with monitoring instead.
rules.action: Remove role exclusions from the MFA policy

rules.headline: Legacy authentication is not blocked tenant-wide
rules.title: Legacy sign-in methods are still allowed
rules.finding: No enabled conditional-access policy blocks legacy authentication for all users on all apps, and legacy protocols cannot use MFA.
rules.why: Legacy protocols such as SMTP and IMAP bypass MFA, so password spraying against them works.
rules.recommendation: Block legacy authentication for all users and apps, with a short, reviewed list of exceptions.
rules.outcome: No MFA bypass through old protocols

rules.headline: {w.log_clearing.events} security-log clears in {w.coverage.archived_days} day(s)
rules.title: Windows security logs are being cleared
rules.finding: {w.log_clearing.events} security-log-cleared events were recorded in {w.coverage.archived_days} archived day(s) ({w.log_clearing.ids_text}); {w.log_clearing.clears_with_no_recorded_actor} have no recorded actor. Windows audit covers {w.coverage.archived_days} of {w.coverage.expected_days} days, so the pattern over the month is {w.pattern_text}.
rules.why: Clearing logs destroys the evidence needed to investigate an attack and makes an attacker's own cleanup look routine.
rules.recommendation: Find what clears the logs and stop it; forward logs off the server and alert on event ID 1102 and 104.
rules.action: Find and stop the security-log clearing; alert on event IDs 1102 and 104

rules.headline: {w.persistence.suspect_count} suspicious new services or tasks
rules.title: Services or tasks with attacker-tool names were installed
rules.finding: {w.persistence.suspect_count} newly installed services or scheduled tasks have names associated with remote-execution or remote-access tools.
rules.why: Ransomware operators install services to run their tools on other machines.
rules.recommendation: Investigate each item and remove any that are not approved.

rules.headline: {r.endpoint.infected} infected devices
rules.title: Devices are currently infected
rules.finding: {r.endpoint.infected} agents report an active infection or active threats.
rules.why: A device with an active threat may already be running attacker code.
rules.recommendation: Isolate each infected device and investigate now.

rules.headline: {r.threats.unresolved_critical} unresolved threats with serious indicators
rules.title: Unresolved threats show credential theft, lateral movement or obfuscation
rules.finding: {r.threats.unresolved_critical} unresolved threats show credential access, lateral movement, obfuscation with other high-risk behaviour, or several open threats on one host.
rules.why: These are the patterns that come before ransomware deployment.
rules.recommendation: Triage them first and isolate the affected hosts.

rules.headline: {r.threats.unmitigated_malicious} malicious threat(s) not mitigated
rules.title: A malicious threat was not mitigated
rules.finding: {r.threats.unmitigated_malicious} threat(s) rated malicious in the last {r.threats.window_days} days were not mitigated.
rules.why: An unmitigated malicious threat may still be active.
rules.recommendation: Contain and investigate each one now.
rules.action: Contain and investigate unmitigated malicious threats

rules.headline: {r.threats.unresolved} threats unresolved
rules.title: Threats remain unresolved
rules.finding: {r.threats.unresolved} threats are not resolved and not marked benign.
rules.why: Open threats may still be active.
rules.recommendation: Close or escalate every open threat.

strengths.text: Confirmed threats are blocked automatically on {r.endpoint.mitigation_modes.protect} of {r.endpoint.agents} agents (Protect mode).
All {r.threats.total} threats in the last {r.threats.window_days} days are resolved.
{r.strong_controls_count} protective settings, for example {r.strong_controls_examples}, are compliant on 95% or more of devices.
Global Administrator accounts are few ({r.identity.global_admins}) and cloud-only.
